summary: Multipart streaming + function call: duplicate partial side-effects after client IP failover
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate partial side-effects (duplicate downstream webhook executions and duplicated DB writes) when a client experiences a network/NAT failover mid-stream while issuing a multipart streaming request that triggers a function/tool call. Impact: data duplication in customer systems, customers observe duplicate invoices created and double notifications. Environment: Dedicated deployment, prod us-east, customer uses a multiplexed TypeScript client behind a corporate NAT that periodically failovers to a new public IP.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a multipart streaming request from the TS SDK that streams user messages and triggers a function call mid-stream (function performs a webhook POST to customer's endpoint).
2) Simulate a client network failover: change public IP / force NAT rebind while stream is active.
3) Client reconnects and retries the stream from last ack.
4) Observe that webhook POST was received twice (partial side-effect executed before retry dedupe prevented).
Notes: customer SDK uses ephemeral per-connection nonce header that is regenerated on reconnect; server-side dedupe header (x-idempotency-key) used only at request start, not per-stream chunk, and webhook handler does not return a dedupe token to client in time before the side-effect executes.
logs:
Client-side (TS SDK) snippet: 
[2026-03-10T09:14:02.123Z] stream.open connectionId=abcd1234 srcIP=52.14.9.33
[2026-03-10T09:14:05.548Z] chunk.sent seq=4 -> function_call(triggerWebhook)
[2026-03-10T09:14:05.552Z] connection.lost reason=TCP_RESET
[2026-03-10T09:14:06.102Z] reconnect.start newConnectionId=efgh5678 srcIP=18.204.22.11
Server logs: 
[2026-03-10T09:14:05.557Z] serving-runtime: function-invoke id=inv-781 status=in-progress target=webhook://customer.example.com/invoice createTx=tx-91
[2026-03-10T09:14:06.110Z] serving-runtime: recovered request from reconnect new-conn=efgh5678 original-stream=abcd1234 resumeAt=4
[2026-03-10T09:14:06.115Z] webhook-handler: POST /invoice id=inv-781 status=200 (processed)
[2026-03-10T09:14:06.200Z] webhook-handler: POST /invoice id=inv-781-replay status=200 (processed)
Observation: two separate webhook events with different internal ids but both executing the same downstream side-effect.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: when the client reconnects with a new connection-level nonce, the server resumes stream processing but does not enforce a request-scoped dedupe token for function calls executed during replay. The function invocation is marked in-flight and the webhook handler processed the first invocation; the resume action retriggered an invocation with a different internal id. We repro'd locally by forcing NAT change and saw identical behavior.
Findings: 
- SDKs create per-connection transient nonce for multiplexed sessions; reconnect loses that nonce.
- Server side resume logic replays unacknowledged chunks without attaching the original idempotency token to the resumed function call if the token lifecycle was tied to the connection.
- Webhook handler has no global dedupe key for these invocations; it relies on caller-provided x-idempotency-key which in this customer's integration was generated by the client at connection start and not persisted across reconnect.
- Workaround surface: ensure client persists a request-level idempotency key across reconnects and include it on every function-invocation chunk. Alternatively, have webhook handler implement dedupe based on application payload (stronger)
resolution:
Short-term workaround provided to customer: 
1) Add a stable per-request idempotency token in the application layer and attach it to every function-call chunk (SDK guidance provided for TS/Python/Go snippets). This token must be persisted across reconnects.
2) Update webhook handler to return a consistent success token and make downstream side-effect idempotent (idempotency-keys in DB + unique constraint on invoice id).
Long-term platform actions proposed: 
- Platform: modify resume behavior to preserve request-scoped idempotency tokens for resumed streams (ENG-3872).
- SDK: add a convenience API to auto-generate persistent request idempotency keys and persist across reconnects (SDK-issue #924).
- Docs: add a new support note and patterns doc for multipart streaming + function calls and network failovers.
Follow-up: PR created for SDK examples and internal ENG ticket created. Customer asked for timeline — we committed to a targeted fix in the platform within 3 sprints and SDK convenience patch in 1 sprint.
